name: py-parse-ini
instruction: Implement parse_ini.py: def parse_ini(text: str) -> dict. Parse an INI-like config into {section: {key: value}}. Keys before any [section] header go into the '' (empty-string) section. Lines starting with ';' or '#' are comments; a '#' INSIDE a value is literal, not a comment. Keys and values are stripped of surrounding whitespace. A repeated key overwrites. A later [section] header merges into the existing section rather than replacing it. A line with no '=' outside a header raises ValueError.
gateCmd: python3 -c "from parse_ini import parse_ini as p; assert p('[a]\\nk=1')=={'a':{'k':'1'}}; print('gate ok')"
